{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Services Agreement (Clear Capital / RadialSpark)

**Document reviewed:** Services Agreement, § 1 Purpose of Engagement et seq.  
**Party posture:** We represent the Customer (Clear Capital / "Company").  
**Prepared by:** In-house counsel  

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **19 findings**: 3 critical deviations/gaps, 6 high, 8 medium and 1 low, with 6 clauses already compliant and 1 item that failed automated review and requires manual attention.

The three critical points are structural. First, § 7 is captioned "INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR" but contains **no operative indemnity language at all** — there is no Vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Second, § 4(a) makes our ownership of the Works **contingent on invoices having been issued and paid**, with no express assignment and no confirmation that we retain ownership of our own data and pre-existing IP. Third, the § 7(a) liability cap is set at fees *actually paid* (Contractor's cap further limited to the individual Statement of Work), with no 12-month look-back, no USD 1,000,000 floor and effectively **no carve-outs** — the sole carve-out cross-references "Paragraph 9", which is the Independent Contractor clause.

Exit and continuity terms are also one-sided: the term is evergreen, our convenience right under § 6(a) is available only when no Statement of Work is outstanding (so we cannot exit an in-flight engagement), while Contractor may walk on 15 days' notice; Contractor may raise rates unilaterally on 30 days' notice with no cap or frequency limit; and there is no transition assistance, data return or deletion obligation anywhere in the Agreement. Governing law (Arizona) and mandatory arbitration are outside our accepted list.

On the positive side, there is **no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum purchase commitment and no liquidated damages or early-termination fee payable by us**; compensation is strictly time-and-materials, and § 1(a) provides that the Agreement controls over conflicting Statement of Work terms.

## Findings

| ID | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary / our position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| f-indemn-d178f051 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | No operative indemnity language exists; § 5(c) non-infringement warranty is capped by § 7(a) and subject to the § 7(c) fee waiver. Insert Vendor indemnity as new § 7(d) (IP, breach of law, data/confidentiality, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with defence procedure and carve-out from the cap and fee waiver. |
| f-ip-adf951f9 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 4 (Ownership of Materials; Acceptance) | Ownership conditioned on invoices issued and paid; no express assignment; embedded-IP licence-back in § 4(c) not irrevocable or worldwide; no Company Data ownership statement. Vest Works on creation via irrevocable assignment, strengthen the licence, add Company Data ownership with no joint ownership. Contractor's retained tools under § 4(b) untouched. |
| f-lol-cap-4db99cd9 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Deviation | § 7 | Cap at fees actually paid, per-SOW for Contractor; no look-back, no USD 1,000,000 floor, no "paid or payable"; only carve-out mis-cross-references Paragraph 9. Make cap mutual at greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, add uncapped Excluded Claims, exclude payment obligations. § 7(b) mutual consequential waiver acceptable. Fallback: 12 months' fees with carve-outs for indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. |
| f-t4c-9f1dc6bd | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 6 (Termination) | Evergreen term; § 6(a) convenience right available only when no SOW is outstanding and no refund of prepaid fees, while Contractor may exit on 15 days' notice. Add a Company 30-day convenience right (including mid-SOW) with refund of prepaid amounts; limit Contractor to 90 days' notice between SOWs. |
| f-license-33da57c6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 4 | § 4(c) licence-back is royalty-free, perpetual and sublicensable but runs to "Company" only, is not stated to be irrevocable, and § 10 arguably blocks transfer to a successor. Add affiliates and contractors, "irrevocable", and successor transferability. |
| f-assign-47014adb | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 7 (operative text at § 10) | § 10 imposes symmetric consent (not unreasonably withheld) — meets fallback only: no affiliate/successor carve-out for us and no bar on assignment to our competitors. § 6 contains no change-of-control trigger. Add the carve-out to the existing sentence plus a confirming sentence; preserve mutual consent otherwise. |
| f-exclusivity-2b0a50f6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) | No exclusivity, sole-source or requirements commitment; § 1(a) engagement is "on a task by task basis". No redline. |
| f-noncompete-add761e1 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 4 | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint on us; § 13 is a mutual, employee-only one-year non-solicit. No redline. |
| f-ld-6ef3a7ef | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties | Compliant | § 6 | No liquidated damages, penalty, late fee, minimum commitment or early-termination fee payable by us; termination limited to accrued fees and expenses. No redline. |
| f-renewal-130e944f | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and pricing | Deviation | § 1 | No auto-renewal (evergreen term; 15-day exit when no SOW outstanding is better than our 30-day opt-out), but § 3(b) gives Contractor an uncapped, unlimited-frequency rate increase on 30 days' notice. Fix rates within each SOW; cap increases at lesser of CPI and 3%, once per 12 months on 60 days' notice (5% fallback). |
| f-transition-da44b0df | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 6 | No transition assistance, data or Confidential Information return, or deletion/certification obligation anywhere. Insert new § 6(c): six months' assistance at then-current rates, return within 30 days in machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter. Fallback: 90 days' assistance. |
| f-warranty-91273c50 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5 (Representations and Warranties; Disclaimer) | Only compliance-with-law, authority, non-infringement and anti-bribery warranties; no conformance warranty, warranty period, no-malicious-code warranty or remedy, while § 5(e) disclaims implied warranties. Add conformance warranty (12 months software / 90 days Services), no-malicious-code warranty and re-perform/repair/replace/refund remedy, and carve the express warranties out of the disclaimer. Fallback: 90/30 days. |
| f-govlaw-29d875f8 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 7 (operative text at §§ 11, 19) | § 11 selects Arizona law (outside our accepted list) and § 19 mandates binding arbitration with no agreed venue. Move to New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County; Delaware or California acceptable as fallback. |
| f-nosolicit-32d65825 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicit binding Customer | Deviation | § 7 (operative text at § 13) | § 13 binds us, so the preferred position is not met, but it is mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, one year post-termination and solicitation-only — substantially our fallback. Add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs; deletion would be disproportionate. |
| f-audit-1e864570 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Needs review** | Not determined | Automated review failed (drafter stopped without submitting a finding). Manual review required before we send comments. |
| f-mfn-8c97d479 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) | No most-favoured-nation, benchmarking or price-matching obligation on us. No redline. |
| f-mincommit-76c60d2f | Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 3 | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume restriction; time-and-materials only and § 1(a) task-by-task. Residual risk sits in individual SOWs, which are not before us; § 1(a) provides the Agreement controls over conflicting SOW terms. No redline. |
| f-insurance-982d8a99 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 7 (operative text at § 14) | Workers' compensation and certificates/notice satisfied; gaps are CGL with no USD 2,000,000 aggregate, E&O at USD 1,000,000 and **no cyber/privacy coverage** despite § 1(c) premises and systems access and § 8 data access. Raise CGL to 1M/2M, E&O to 2M, add cyber, extend one year post-term at Contractor's expense. Fallback: E&O 1M (already met) plus cyber 2M. |

## Walk-away items

These sit at or near the playbook walk-away line and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (f-indemn-d178f051, critical).** The absence of any Contractor IP indemnity is expressly the playbook walk-away position. We need the new § 7(d) indemnity, with defence of third-party claims and carve-out from the § 7(a) cap and § 7(c) attorneys' fee waiver.
2. **Effective "AS IS" delivery (f-warranty-91273c50, medium but walk-away in substance).** Because § 5(e) puts the express warranties in lieu of all implied warranties and nothing conformance-related replaces them, we are close to the walk-away "AS IS" position. A conformance warranty with a remedy is required.
3. **No cyber/privacy insurance (f-insurance-982d8a99).** A vendor with facility access under § 1(c) and access to our data and Confidential Information under § 8, carrying no cyber coverage, sits at the walk-away line. Cyber is the element we most need; the limit is negotiable, the coverage is not.

We also flag, without treating as walk-away, that the § 7(a) cap as drafted can fall far below the playbook minimum and that the sole carve-out cross-reference is inoperative — this should be resolved in the same pass as the indemnity.

## Next steps

1. **Complete the AUDIT review** (f-audit-1e864570) manually before issuing comments, so the mark-up is complete on first exchange.
2. **Issue the redline** in the priority order: (i) the three critical items — Vendor indemnity, ownership/assignment of Works and Company Data, and the liability cap with carve-outs; (ii) exit and continuity — Company convenience termination, transition assistance and data return, and the rate-increase cap; (iii) licence scope, assignment carve-out, governing law and venue, non-solicit carve-outs, and insurance limits.
3. **Correct the drafting defects** we noted while marking up: the inoperative "Paragraph 9" cross-reference in § 7(a), the mis-numbered § 7(c) termination limb, and the § 4 "ACCEPTANCE" heading with no acceptance mechanics.
4. **Signal the fallbacks** in our comments where sensible — 12 months' fees with core carve-outs on the cap; 90 days' transition assistance; 90/30-day warranty periods; Delaware or California law; E&O at USD 1,000,000 plus cyber at USD 2,000,000 — to shorten the negotiation.
5. **Request the Statements of Work** referenced in § 1(a). Our minimum-commitment and pricing conclusions depend on SOW terms we have not seen; § 1(a)'s precedence language helps, but we should confirm the SOWs do not reintroduce commitments or fees.
6. **Confirm the compliant positions are not traded away** in later drafts: no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum commitment and no Customer-payable liquidated damages."}
